title: Snapshot USA 2019-2023: weekly camera-trap detections of 87 mammal species at 9,694 deployments in 263 arrays across the United States
creator: Rooney, Brigit; McShea, William J.; Kays, Roland; Cove, Michael V.; and the Snapshot USA contributors
citation: Rooney, B., McShea, W. J., Kays, R., Cove, M. V., et al. (2025). SNAPSHOT USA 2019-2023: The first five years of data from a coordinated camera trap survey of the United States [Data set]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.k0p2ngfhn (version 3, 2025-01-03)
abstract: Snapshot USA is an annual, multi-contributor camera-trap survey of mammals across the United States, run each autumn (deployments between 1 August and 29 December) since 2019 with a shared protocol: arrays of about ten cameras per site type, cameras run for several weeks, images identified in Wildlife Insights to species where possible. This table aggregates the 2019-2023 sequence file to camera-weeks: one row per deployment x 7-day window x species for the 87 mammal species with at least 50 sequences over the five years, y = detected in that week, y_raw = number of sequences, obs_camera_days = days of the window inside the deployment (the last window is partial). The deployment table is the survey set. Camera coordinates are coarsened to 0.1-degree cell centres and deployment, array, site and project names replaced by sequential ids because two shipped species are IUCN flagged (red wolf CR, giant kangaroo rat EN); rooney_2025_snapshotusa_exact_comm has the other 85 species at published precision. Built from Dryad version 3 (2025-01-03); the current version 6 is not downloadable without a token.
samplingProtocol: Unbaited passive-infrared camera traps at knee height facing trails or random points, 10+ cameras per array spaced >= 200 m, run for several weeks between August and December; sequences = photos within one minute of a trigger; species identified by the contributors in Wildlife Insights
occasionLength: 7 days (last window of a deployment partial)
surveyEvidenceNote: A camera-day exists iff Start_Date <= day <= End_Date in ssusa_alldeployments.csv (Survey_Nights = End - Start for every row); camera-days are grouped into 7-day windows from the start date. Every sequence in the file falls inside its deployment's window; 27 sequence rows naming a deployment absent from the deployments file are dropped.
closureNote: period = survey year (one deployment per unit, so a unit has rows in one period only); occasion = camera-week within the deployment, 1-21 weeks
geographicCoverage: United States (all 50 states), camera coordinates coarsened to 0.1-degree cells; latitude 21.4 to 59.5, longitude -157.7 to -68.6

coordinatesCoarsened.method: 0.1-degree grid cell centre for every deployment (one unit set serves all taxa); red wolf (Canis rufus, IUCN CR) and giant kangaroo rat (Dipodomys ingens, IUCN EN) are among the shipped taxa; the source publishes exact camera coordinates (WGS 84, 4-6 decimals); deployment ids, array names, site names and project names replaced by sequential ids or not shipped (E7.4)

covariateNote: unit_habitat and unit_development_level are the contributors' array-level classifications as deposited; a sequential site_id (linking deployments of one site across years), Feature_Type and the deployment dates are in __units.
designNote: Community detection table aggregated to camera-weeks (E9 core). The deposit is sequence-level with timestamps, so daily or finer occasions can be rebuilt from the source; weeks were chosen to keep the table at 5.1 million rows. period duplicates unit_year because the survey is an annual design with new deployments each year; a dynamic model across years needs the site, not the deployment, as the unit (site_id in __units; 6,712 sites, most sampled in several years).
notes: Taxa are the 87 mammal species with >= 50 sequences; the 43 mammal species below that cut are not shipped (see notShipped). 46 Deployment_IDs recur in two years and carry a _<year> suffix in unit. The deposit's version 3 is used (see abstract). y_raw counts distinct Sequence_IDs (a sequence with two rows for one species, e.g. age/sex groups, counts once); on 223 deployments (14,445 rows) the Sequence_ID is NA and each row's start time stands in for it.
